title: Student gradebook with statistics, ranking and CSV import/export
prompt:
Build a student gradebook in Python.

Modules:
- grading.py: `letter_grade(score) -> str` returns `A` for 90 and above, `B` for 80-89.99, `C` for 70-79.99, `D` for 60-69.99 and `F` below 60.
- gradebook.py: `class GradeBook`.
  - `add_student(name)` raises `ValueError` if the student already exists.
  - `add_grade(name, subject, score)` records a score; raises `KeyError` for an unknown student and `ValueError` if score is not between 0 and 100 inclusive.
  - `average(name) -> float` is the mean of all that student's scores; raises `ValueError` if the student has no grades.
  - `subject_average(subject) -> float` is the mean of all scores recorded for that subject; raises `ValueError` if there are none.
  - `ranking() -> list[str]` returns student names ordered by average (highest first), ties broken alphabetically. Students with no grades are left out.
  - `to_csv(path)` writes every grade to a CSV file with the header row `name,subject,score`.
  - `GradeBook.from_csv(path)` (a classmethod) reads such a file and returns a GradeBook containing those students and grades.
- main.py: command-line interface. Read commands from standard input, one per line, until `quit` or end of input:
  - `student <name>`
  - `grade <name> <subject> <score>`
  - `report` prints one line per ranked student: `<rank>. <name> <average with 1 decimal> <letter grade of the average>`, e.g. `1. alice 91.5 A`
  - On any error print a line starting with `Error:` and continue.

Constraints: use only the Python standard library. The entry point is main.py in the project root, guarded by `if __name__ == "__main__":`.
smoke_stdin:
student alice
grade alice math 90
report
quit
